headline: Southborough officials began planning a potential five-year operating tax override for FY28 while adopting higher transfer station fees and advancing key zoning and school reviews.
synopsis: Town officials initiated early planning for fiscal year 2028, debating a potential multi-year Proposition 2 1/2 operational override to address a projected $2 million deficit. The Select Board approved higher transfer station permit fees for FY27 to cover operational expenses and contracted hauling costs. Consultants delivered an existing conditions evaluation for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School outlining substantial renovation needs for HVAC, windows, and accessibility ahead of 2027 Town Meeting. The Zoning Board of Appeals granted height and setback variances for the proposed Costco development at 21 Coslin Drive and approved a draft bylaw updating two-family housing rules. Meanwhile, the Board of Health adopted updated well and septic regulations, and town committees refined Community Preservation Act requests for parks, trails, and golf course infrastructure.

top_items.title: FY28 budget forecasting and potential Proposition 2 1/2 override
top_items.why: Town boards began evaluating a projected $2 million deficit for fiscal year 2028, discussing a potential five-year operational tax override of up to $10 million.
top_items.body: The Select Board reviewed long-range budget forecasts showing that Southborough faces an estimated $2 million deficit in FY28 that would exhaust remaining tax levy capacity. Following advice from state Division of Local Services advisors, town leaders discussed pursuing a five-year operational override to build excess levy capacity rather than holding annual votes. The Advisory Committee subsequently evaluated the concept, weighing the merits of a five-year, $10 million authorization against single-year overrides, before setting a joint session with the Select Board for August 11.

top_items.title: Select Board increases FY27 transfer station permit fees
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 5-0 to adopt higher transfer station permit fees to offset hauling costs and operating expenses.
top_items.body: To address operational costs, including $62,000 in temporary contracted hauling while municipal staff acquire commercial driver's licenses, the Select Board approved Option 2 sticker pricing. Under the new rate structure, the first standard permit is set at $320, second permits at $25, senior permits at $75, and second senior permits at $25, with hardship permits waived at $0. Proposed operational regulations concerning swap shop drop-offs and disposal of bulky items were deferred to August 11.

top_items.title: Neary Elementary baseline conditions analysis and project timeline
top_items.why: Architects outlined extensive facility deficiencies at Margaret A. Neary Elementary School targeting a major renovation or replacement proposal for 2027 Town Meeting.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects delivered an initial conditions assessment of Margaret A. Neary Elementary School to the Elementary School Building Committee. While the building structure is sound, consultants found it needs comprehensive modernization, including triple-glazed windows, improved wall insulation, full accessibility compliance, automatic fire suppression sprinklers, and new HVAC systems to replace noisy unit ventilators. The committee discussed modular classroom conditions and options for educational programming, with plans to present refined alternatives to voters at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Costco granted variances for retaining walls and parking lighting
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 4-0 to approve variance relief for 31-foot retaining walls and 36.5-foot parking light poles at 21 Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: Costco Wholesale Corporation secured variance relief from the Zoning Board of Appeals to prepare the former Dell campus site. Variances permit retaining walls up to 31 feet high in yard setbacks to manage a 40-foot grade change and create a level parking lot. The board also authorized light poles reaching 36 feet 6 inches, exceeding the town's 20-foot zoning limit, after the applicant demonstrated that taller poles would reduce the total pole count from 113 to 49 while maintaining zero light trespass beyond property lines.

top_items.title: ZBA endorses draft two-family zoning bylaw amendment
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved a draft zoning amendment clarifying regulations and removing conversion barriers for two-family homes.
top_items.body: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted 4-0 to advance proposed zoning revisions defining two-family dwellings, separating them from single-family homes with accessory dwelling units, and removing an obsolete two-year waiting requirement for conversions. The draft also adjusts minimum lot sizes across commercial and residential zoning districts. The proposal was forwarded to the Select Board for referral to the Planning Board ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Board of Health approves revised well and septic regulations
top_items.why: The Board of Health voted unanimously to adopt stricter rules for septic system designers, mandatory pre-sale well tests, and setbacks.
top_items.body: Following a public hearing, the Board of Health enacted updated regulations governing subsurface sewage disposal systems and private drinking wells. The revised rules require independent separation between septic designers and installers, mandate guaranteed access easements for future septic repairs, establish a 25-foot separation between private wells and swimming pools, and introduce mandatory drinking water quality testing before real estate transactions.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge budget revised for CPA funding
top_items.why: The Trails Committee finalized a $226,096 CPA funding request for a reservoir footbridge after removing a costly boardwalk section.
top_items.body: Following bids that came in higher than expected, the Trails Committee redesigned the Peninsula Trail connection over the Stony Brook reservoir channel by eliminating the proposed boardwalk component in favor of an upland dirt path. The adjusted project budget totals $434,328 to $437,328, pairing existing unspent funds with a new Community Preservation Act request presented to the Community Preservation Committee ahead of Special Town Meeting.
